item.title: Bird-watchers flock to symphony of swirling ducks
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-18
A dark smudge appears above the horizon, then it becomes a line, and eventually a massive flying wave. Within seconds, the sky above Shandong Yellow River Delta National Nature Reserve appears to be alive, swelling and swirling with more than a quarter of a million birds flying as if they share a single nervous system. British birdwatcher Paul Holt has watched birds for more than 50 years. He has seen intricate murmurations in Europe and Asia. But standing on the mudflat at dusk, he does not try to rank this one. "The flock gets up and they move about, and they don't crash into each other," he said. "It's amazing. It's really spectacular." The birds are Baikal teals, small ducks with patterned faces, and they are the swell driving the "bird wave". The reserve's monitoring put the single species flock at over 280,000 on Monday — a record for the site. Zhao Yajie, deputy director of the reserve's ecological monitoring center, has watched the number of ducks climb over the years from a few thousand, to 40,000, to 170,000, and now past 200,000. The ducks roost in the reserve's wetlands during the day and fly out to feed along the riverbanks at night. At dawn and dusk, they move between the two, and the crossing is what visitors come to see. The flight lasts 15 to 25 minutes, sometimes less. Holt first came to Dongying years ago and has returned four times. He calls the Yellow River Delta one of the most spectacular birdwatching sites he has seen.

item.title: One language, countless possibilities
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-18
Dressed in traditional qipao and sporting plush panda charms, young people from around the world greeted one another with a cheerful ni hao (hello) as they gathered at the China National Convention Center in Beijing. Some were meeting for the first time, while others were catching up with old friends, sharing stories about their studies, career plans and experiences in China. Among them was Edward John O'Brien III, a 27-year-old from the United States who began learning Chinese at 13. He earned a master's degree in international trade from Southwestern University of Finance and Economics in Chengdu, Sichuan province, and has lived in China for more than two years. "Learning Chinese has given me many opportunities to make the most of my strengths in self-expression," he said. "I plan to set my sights on media production, cultural exchange projects, and social media content creation in China." O'Brien was among about 5,000 participants from more than 160 countries and regions attending the 2026 World Chinese Language Conference, held in Beijing from Nov 13 to 15 under the theme "Chinese: More Than a Language". Hosted by China's Ministry of Education, the conference brought together education officials, scholars, teachers and business representatives for eight specialized forums exploring the future of international Chinese education and global cooperation. At the conference's plenary session, Minister of Education Huai Jinpeng highlighted the growing global significance of Chinese, not only as a means of communication but also as a driver of economic development and a bridge between civilizations. Global interest in Chinese continued to grow this year, with the number of people overseas learning and using the language reaching 210 million. Meanwhile, participation in the Chinese Proficiency Test (HSK), a standardized assessment of Chinese language proficiency, exceeded 1 million for the first time in 2026, according to figures released at the World Chinese Language Conference. For young learners, these figures reflect possibilities that extend far beyond the classroom. The Chinese Bridge competition has helped young learners turn their language studies into meaningful international exchanges. This year marked the 25th anniversary of the event, which has attracted more than 1.8 million young participants from over 160 countries and regions. Cameron Patterson of the United Kingdom took second place in the 14th Chinese Bridge competition in 2015. "Learning a language is not just about mastering a tool for communication. More importantly, it allows us to build connections, participate in different cultural activities, and encounter people and experiences we might otherwise never have known," he said. Over the years, Patterson has witnessed growing interest in Chinese language and culture in the UK, with more schools incorporating Chinese into their curricula. Beyond cultural exchange and personal growth, Chinese proficiency is also becoming a valuable professional asset, particularly in countries with expanding economic ties to China. For Moussa Ousmane Mahaman Sani, a master's student from Niger at the China University of Petroleum (Beijing), learning Chinese could open doors to a career in his country's energy sector. Energy cooperation between China and Niger has expanded in recent years. In 2024, Niger signed a memorandum of understanding with China National Petroleum Corp (CNPC) concerning crude oil sales from the Agadem oilfield. "We have deep cooperation with China," Mahaman Sani said. "If I can speak Chinese, I gain a competitive edge in my home country's job market." As he prepares to complete his master's degree in 2027, Sani is considering further study and career paths that would allow him to contribute to China-Niger energy partnerships.

item.title: China, APEC partners sail toward shared prosperity
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-18
At the APEC media center in Shenzhen, Guangdong province, nine digital flip screens rise like sails from a boat-shaped base. The installation, called "Asia-Pacific Sails", draws inspiration from a maritime image that President Xi Jinping evoked 13 years ago: the region's economies sailing forward together across a shared sea. "Boundless is the ocean where we sail with the wind," Xi said at the APEC CEO Summit in Bali, Indonesia, in 2013. Since then, Xi has attended or chaired successive Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation Economic Leaders' Meetings, putting forward ideas, initiatives and proposals aimed at steering regional cooperation toward greater openness, shared development and mutual benefit. The 33rd APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting will open in Shenzhen on Wednesday, marking the third time that China has hosted the gathering, following Shanghai in 2001 and Beijing in 2014. Under the theme "Building an Asia-Pacific Community to Prosper Together", this year's APEC agenda centers on three priorities: openness, innovation and cooperation. A consistent message in Xi's addresses over the years has been that China's door to the world will not close, but will only open wider. At the APEC CEO Summit in Lima, Peru, in 2016, Xi emphasized that China is committed to a win-win strategy of opening-up. While striving for its own development, China would also work to promote the common development of all Asia-Pacific countries and create more opportunities for people in the region, he said. Addressing the APEC CEO Dialogues in November 2020, Xi underscored that openness is important to a nation's development, saying that economic globalization was irreversible and no country could develop itself by keeping its doors closed. Since China joined APEC 35 years ago, it has become increasingly integrated into the regional economy, with trade and investment ties linking its development ever more closely to that of Asia-Pacific economies. China is now the largest trading partner of 13 APEC economies, while eight of its top 10 trading partners are APEC members. Those ties have continued to deepen. In the first three quarters of 2026, China's trade in goods with other APEC economies rose 23.9 percent year-on-year to 24.07 trillion yuan ($3.6 trillion), accounting for 60.3 percent of its total foreign trade. Alongside expanding trade, China has continued to widen market access and pursue institutional reforms for further opening-up. It has reduced its national negative list for foreign investment access to 29 items, removed all manufacturing-sector restrictions for foreign investment and expanded pilot programs for opening up the services sector. Dun Zhigang, a senior research fellow at Renmin University of China's Chongyang Institute for Financial Studies, said China's opening-up increasingly extends beyond market access to encompass rules, regulations, management and standards. Noting China's economic scale, manufacturing capabilities and role in supply chains, Gulnar Shaimergenova, director of the China Studies Center in Kazakhstan, said although Kazakhstan is not an APEC member, developments in the Asia-Pacific affect its economy through trade, investment and transportation. Alongside openness, Xi has consistently emphasized innovation as a driving force for Asia-Pacific growth and the importance of ensuring that its benefits are widely shared. At the 2013 APEC CEO Summit, he identified reform, readjustment and innovation as sources of renewed growth momentum. Five years later, at the APEC CEO Summit in Port Moresby, Papua New Guinea, Xi warned that scientific and technological innovations should not be locked up or become profit-making tools for a few. He called for an environment of international cooperation that would deliver the fruit of innovation to more nations. That emphasis on broadening access to innovation has taken on new significance with the rapid development of artificial intelligence. At the second session of the 2025 APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting in Gyeongju, South Korea, Xi called for deeper cooperation on open-source technologies and said China was ready to work with other APEC members to enhance AI literacy and bridge the region's digital and AI divide. China has also led the establishment of the World Artificial Intelligence Cooperation Organization to strengthen international cooperation on AI development and governance. In July, China announced it would establish a center in Shenzhen's Qianhai area, providing a platform to promote APEC cooperation on cross-border data flows to support the region's digital development. Lan Qingxin, director of the BRICS Research Center of the University of International Business and Economics said that policy exchanges, technical support and training could help developing economies participate more fully in digital transformation and industrial upgrading. He called for greater technological cooperation and demonstration projects under APEC to help innovations move from experimentation to wider application. Shenzhen's development offers valuable experience in how opening-up and institutional reform can translate investment and innovation into industrial strength, Lan said. Jaspal Kaur Sadhu Singh, an associate professor at Canterbury Christ Church University in the United Kingdom, said China's experience could help emerging economies strengthen their own technological capabilities. Other economies could draw lessons from China's application and governance of AI, while adapting those lessons to their own values, needs and circumstances, she said. Paul Triolo, an honorary senior fellow on technology at the Asia Society Policy Institute's Center for China Analysis, said he expected discussions in Shenzhen to explore how governments could encourage innovation while establishing regulatory safeguards against the risks associated with AI. At the APEC chairmanship handover session in Gyeongju in November 2025, Xi said China was ready to use its role as APEC host to work with other members toward building an Asia-Pacific community and promoting regional growth and prosperity. He pledged to advance practical cooperation in a wide range of areas, with the aim of injecting fresh momentum into regional development and delivering greater benefits to people. That commitment has been reflected in the agenda of China's APEC host year, during which it has held more than 300 meetings and events with other members. In a signed article published on Monday, Foreign Minister Wang Yi said China would use the APEC leaders' declaration to draw up a road map for building an Asia-Pacific community and establish a framework for collective action. The Shenzhen meeting also comes as 2026 marks the 20th anniversary of the vision for a Free Trade Area of the Asia-Pacific and the year of the final evaluation of the APEC Connectivity Blueprint for 2015-2025. Wang said China would work to develop a framework document on trade digitalization cooperation and a new connectivity cooperation document based on the final review of the APEC Connectivity Blueprint. The push for closer cooperation comes at a time when geopolitical tensions and differences in development are posing challenges to regional integration. John Ross, a British economist, said APEC has demonstrated that economies with different political systems and levels of development can prioritize economic growth and pursue cooperation without setting aside differences. APEC operates through consensus and voluntary, nonbinding commitments, allowing economies with diverse interests to pursue cooperation at their own pace. Dun, the researcher at Renmin University of China, said this approach could help members manage disagreements and find common ground while respecting their stages of development and interests. Du Lan, deputy director of the China Institute of International Studies' Department for Asia-Pacific Studies, said that building an Asia-Pacific community could help to safeguard regional strategic stability amid growing pressures to form rival blocs. By putting common development at the center of regional cooperation, such a community could help economies avoid being forced to choose sides and preserve the strategic autonomy of smaller economies, she said. Guy Ryder, United Nations under-secretary-general for policy, said APEC provides an important opportunity for dialogue among influential international players. He expressed hope that the forum would help advance the UN Sustainable Development Goals and complement the world body's efforts to address shared challenges. zhaojia@chinadaily.com.cn

item.title: Xi and Carney agree to boost Sino-Canadian ties
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-18
President Xi Jinping called on China and Canada to build on the momentum of improving bilateral ties, deepen cooperation in traditional and emerging sectors and expand people-to-people exchanges during talks with Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney on Tuesday. Carney arrived in the coastal city of Shenzhen, South China's Guangdong province, on Monday, for his second visit to China this year as prime minister, following his first in January. Xi said improving and developing relations between China and Canada, both important Asia-Pacific countries, serve their peoples' interests and contribute to world peace, stability, development and prosperity. The course of bilateral relations has underscored the importance of mutual respect, equality and mutual benefit, and the seeking of common ground while reserving differences, he said. To develop bilateral ties, Xi called on the two sides to build on the current momentum and strengthen political mutual trust. Through constructive dialogue and communication, the two sides should foster a more accurate understanding of each other's development paths and policy intentions, deepen their understanding of and respect for each other's core interests and major concerns, and properly manage and resolve differences to jointly keep bilateral relations on the right course, he said. Xi urged closer alignment to deepen cooperation in traditional areas such as trade and energy and expand cooperation in emerging sectors including the green economy, drawing on complementary strengths for mutual benefit. Carney said bilateral ties had been on the right track since the new strategic partnership was established earlier this year. Substantial trade growth and progress across sectors demonstrated that cooperation could deepen on the basis of mutual respect, he said. mojingxi@chinadaily.com.cn

item.title: Mutual respect enables stable partnership with Chile
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-18
President Xi Jinping said on Tuesday that China and Chile should work together to be partners of mutual respect and trust, pioneers of all-round cooperation, defenders of the common interests of developing countries and promoters of China-Latin America cooperation. Xi made the remarks during a meeting with Chilean President Jose Antonio Kast in Shenzhen. He said that the China-Chile relationship has withstood the test of the changes of the international landscape, maintaining long-term healthy and stable development and standing at the forefront of China's relations with South American countries. The most important experience drawn from the growth of China-Chile ties is that both countries respect each other, treat each other as equals and adhere to mutual respect and seek win-win results, he added. Xi underlined the need for both countries to continue to support each other on issues concerning their core interests and major concerns, strengthen exchanges at all levels and in various fields, and promote exchanges on governance experience. Noting that China and Chile have complementary economic structures and a strong foundation for cooperation, he called on both sides to strengthen the alignment of development strategies through high-quality Belt and Road cooperation, enhance collaboration in traditional fields. He also expressed the country's willingness to work with Latin American and Caribbean countries to inject more certainty into peace and development in the region. Kast said that for many years, China has been Chile's largest trading partner and the largest export destination for its agricultural products and minerals, and cooperation with China has provided important opportunities for Chile's economic and social development. caodesheng@chinadaily.com.cn

item.title: Collaboration with Peru has scope for further elevation
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-18
President Xi Jinping called on China and Peru on Tuesday to strengthen cooperation in infrastructure, energy and resources, and tap the potential for collaboration in emerging areas such as new energy and artificial intelligence to achieve shared prosperity. Xi made the remarks during a meeting with Peruvian President Keiko Fujimori in Shenzhen, Guangdong province. Noting that this year marks the 55th anniversary of diplomatic relations between the two countries, he said China has been Peru's largest trading partner and largest export destination for 12 consecutive years. He noted that the Chancay Port, built with the participation of Chinese enterprises, has given a strong boost to economic and trade cooperation between Asia and Latin America. China is ready to work with Peru to take their comprehensive strategic partnership to new heights and bring greater benefits to both peoples, Xi said. He called for closer friendly exchanges between the two countries' governments, legislative bodies, political parties and at the subnational level to strengthen political mutual trust. The two sides should continue unlocking the benefits from the protocol upgrading the bilateral free trade agreement, which took effect on Nov 1, he said. The two countries should strengthen multilateral cooperation and enhance communication and coordination within frameworks including the United Nations and the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation to uphold true multilateralism and free trade, and jointly safeguard international fairness and justice, he added. Fujimori said Peru firmly adheres to the one-China principle and hopes to expand exchanges between the two peoples and advance cooperation in trade, investment and infrastructure. zhaojia@chinadaily.com.cn

item.title: President focuses on greater depth of relations with Mexico
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-18
China stands ready to work with Mexico to steer bilateral ties toward high-quality development and jointly promote an Asia-Pacific that is prosperous and stable, open and interconnected, universally beneficial and inclusive, united and mutually supportive, President Xi Jinping said on Tuesday. In talks with Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum Pardo in Shenzhen, Guangdong province, Xi stressed joint efforts to work toward a fairer and more equitable global governance system and contribute to world peace and common development. Xi said that advancing China-Mexico relations to a higher level and expanding cooperation in both scope and depth is of great significance to the development of both countries and greater solidarity among Global South nations. The president called on China and Mexico to deepen political mutual trust, strengthen exchanges and cooperation at all levels and across various fields, and jointly ensure the success of celebrations next year marking the 55th anniversary of diplomatic relations. He urged both sides to pursue mutually beneficial cooperation, better align their development strategies and expand collaboration in infrastructure, science and technology, clean energy, culture and tourism. Xi also called for closer coordination at the United Nations and other multilateral platforms to uphold fairness and justice and safeguard the basic norms governing international relations. Sheinbaum said that Mexico firmly adheres to the one-China principle and attaches great importance to its relations with China. Mexico, which will host the APEC meetings in 2028, is willing to strengthen multilateral coordination with China, uphold multilateralism and safeguard the common interests of the Global South, she added. jihaisheng@chinadaily.com.cn

item.title: Regional development, connectivity stressed
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-18
Editor's note: President Xi Jinping held six bilateral talks with leaders attending the APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting in Shenzhen, Guangdong province, on Tuesday. President Xi Jinping called on Tuesday for China and Vietnam to enhance mutual trust and solidarity, deepen comprehensive cooperation, and jointly safeguard peace and stability and promote development and prosperity. Xi, who is also general secretary of the Communist Party of China Central Committee, made the remarks during a meeting with General Secretary of the Communist Party of Vietnam Central Committee and Vietnamese President To Lam in Shenzhen. He described China and Vietnam as "comrades and brothers", saying that "the rougher the seas, the more we must pull together". While calling for promoting the alignment of their interests, Xi underlined the need for both countries to boost connectivity, advance the early establishment of smart ports and cross-border economic cooperation zones, expand collaboration in digital transformation and green, low-carbon development, and explore partnership in applications of artificial intelligence. He called on both sides to properly manage their differences in the South China Sea issue, steadily advance maritime cooperation, and strengthen cooperation within frameworks such as the United Nations, China-ASEAN cooperation, and Lancang-Mekong cooperation. Xi also expressed China's willingness to strengthen mutual learning with Vietnam in development experiences, firmly support each other, and deepen exchanges on party self-supervision and self-governance. To Lam expressed his congratulations on the successful convening of the fifth plenary session of the 20th CPC Central Committee. He said that Vietnam highly values its relationship with China, and regards it as its most important strategic partner. In the current complex international situation, Vietnam is willing to strengthen solidarity and cooperation with China to aid each other's development, he added. caodesheng@chinadaily.com.cn
